Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like April 2022. Headline CPI is 8.52% YoY, which matches the March 2022 print released in April. The unemployment rate is 3.6%, and the fed funds rate averaged about 1.58%, which fits May 2022 better than April. But CPI of 8.52% is the March figure, and the April CPI was 8.26%.

Checking the other readings against the calendar:
- The 10-year yield is 3.10% and the 2-year is 3.06%. In May 2022 the 10-year ended near 2.85%, and it was about 3.0% in mid-June. At the end of April it was about 2.89%. A 10-year at 3.10% fits mid-June 2022, or a snapshot for June.
- The fed funds rate at 1.58% fits June 2022 (effective rate 1.21% in June, then 1.68% in July). The 3-month change of +1.25 suggests a rise from about 0.33% in March, which gives 1.58% in June. That fits June.
- CPI of 8.52% does not match the May print of 8.56% exactly, though it is close. Core CPI of 6.01% is close to the May figure of 6.0%.
- US large-cap equity is down 8.2% over 1 month and 20.4% from its 12-month high, which fits June 2022. The S&P was down about 8.4% in June.
- The VIX at 28.16 is also consistent with June 2022.
- The unemployment rate of 3.6% and the 3-month average payroll gain of 408k both fit May 2022.

My estimate is June 2022.
